title: Praggnanandhaa Bounces Back at Sinquefield Cup With Win Over Van Foreest
excerpt: The Indian grandmaster rebounds from a Round 3 loss to Keymer, defeating Jorden van Foreest in Round 4 to sit half a point behind tournament leader Wesley So.
body:
• Praggnanandhaa defeated Jorden van Foreest in Round 4 of the 2026 Sinquefield Cup, inflicting the Dutchman's third consecutive loss
  • Wesley So leads the tournament with 3/4 after four rounds, half a point ahead of Praggnanandhaa, Aronian, and Vachier-Lagrave
  • Praggnanandhaa's Round 4 win follows a 95-move victory over World Championship challenger Sindarov in Round 2 and a loss to Keymer in Round 3
  • The Sinquefield Cup is the final leg of the 2026 Grand Chess Tour, with the top-four players qualifying for the Grand Chess Tour Finals

R Praggnanandhaa scored a clinical victory over Jorden van Foreest in Round 4 of the 2026 Sinquefield Cup in Saint Louis on Wednesday, recovering from a painful loss to Vincent Keymer the previous round. The win moves Praggnanandhaa to 2.5/4, half a point behind tournament leader Wesley So.

Van Foreest, who has now lost three of his four games, fell into trouble early when he accepted a pawn sacrifice from Praggnanandhaa on move eight. "This was like one of 10 things I looked at," Praggnanandhaa told the audience after the game, admitting he had to take time to remember his preparation after Van Foreest grabbed the pawn.

A Queen Sacrifice Seals the Deal

The game exploded when Van Foreest sacrificed his queen, leaving Praggnanandhaa with a decisive material advantage. "The good thing about this position is I can never be worse," Praggnanandhaa said. He converted the endgame of queen versus rook with precision, later joking about the technical challenge: "If I can't win this, I shouldn't be playing at this level!"

A Rollercoaster Four Rounds

Praggnanandhaa's Sinquefield Cup campaign has been anything but dull. After a quiet draw in Round 1, he outplayed World Championship challenger Javokhir Sindarov in Round 2, grinding out a 95-move endgame victory. "We barely have draws... Javokhir is someone who pushes to the end and I enjoy going for it as well," Praggnanandhaa said of the matchup, according to Chess.com.

Round 3 brought his first setback when Keymer bounced back from his own Round 2 loss to Aronian and defeated the Indian grandmaster. But Praggnanandhaa responded immediately with the Round 4 win over Van Foreest.

The rest of Round 4 saw draws across the board. The marquee matchup between Aronian and So ended in a threefold repetition after 32 moves in a Berlin Defense. Aronian joked about his restraint, quoting his second Aryan Tari: "Don't do stupid things like you did before!" Vachier-Lagrave drew with Keymer, Giri held Sindarov, and Sevian pressed Caruana in a long endgame but could not break through.

Grand Chess Tour Finals Race Heats Up

The $475,000 Sinquefield Cup is the fifth and final leg of the 2026 Grand Chess Tour, with the top-four players across all events qualifying for the Grand Chess Tour Finals. Coming into the Sinquefield Cup, Caruana led the overall standings with 25 points, followed by Praggnanandhaa on 24.5, So on 23.5, and Keymer on 21.

Praggnanandhaa arrives at this tournament riding momentum from his maiden title at the 2026 Saint Louis Rapid & Blitz, where he won $50,000 and led from start to finish. A strong finish at the Sinquefield Cup would all but guarantee his spot in the Grand Chess Tour Finals.

What's Next

Round 5 on Friday, August 14, features a marquee clash between tournament leader So and the in-form Praggnanandhaa. A rest day follows on Saturday before the tournament resumes. Five rounds remain in the nine-round event, which concludes on August 19.
